label: Stack
title: Stack
summary: Use Stack when a public component slot needs one token-driven gap and an intentional vertical or horizontal direction.
corePrinciple: Choose direction from the content role. Stack stays direction-locked; it does not switch because the viewport changed.

anatomy.title: Stack has one job
anatomy.description: See the slot, direction, gap, and cross-axis fit that make Stack useful.
blocks: Set layoutDirection to vertical or horizontal. The default is vertical.
Slot gap provides repeated separation. Stack has no padding, wrap, or reverse control.
fillWidth makes these vertical children share the host edge. Fixed child dimensions still win.

anatomy.note: Set layoutDirection to vertical or horizontal. The default is vertical.
Slot gap provides repeated separation. Stack has no padding, wrap, or reverse control.
fillWidth makes these vertical children share the host edge. Fixed child dimensions still win.

configuration.title: Configure the owner, then read the result
configuration.description: Set direction and cross-axis behavior for the public slot that owns this Stack.
blocks: Use the default direction for a column of actions or supporting content inside a public slot.
Use a row when sibling actions or content belong on one line. Direction is explicit.
equalHeight stretches a horizontal row; fillWidth stretches a vertical column. Fixed child sizes still win.
Use only for the active direction
Use Stack through a public component slot

Stack is a public JFS export and a documented layout primitive. The Figma source is a Coin Subcomponents anatomy reference, so designers should consume public components and patterns that own the slot.

states.title: Stack responds to its host
states.description: Compare default, changed rhythm, host-owned edge, and constrained outcomes without recreating the layout primitive.
blocks: Default column direction for grouped slot content.
Explicit row direction for sibling content.
Horizontal children share the tallest height when they can stretch.
Vertical children stretch across the stack when they can.
Stack does not add overlap, z-order, wrapping, padding, or automatic viewport switching. Use the public component that owns the slot.

sizing.title: The parent supplies the constraint
sizing.description: Stack keeps its chosen direction at every width. Responsive intent belongs to the owning public composition.
blocks: Stack keeps the configured direction in both hosts. Choose a different public composition when the content role changes; the viewport does not switch layoutDirection for you.

content.title: Make the relationship visible
content.description: Stack works when a public slot has a clear group and direction.
blocks: Use Stack for a clear group such as actions, metadata, or supporting copy.
Direction expresses the content relationship and remains stable through viewport changes.
Use equalHeight for a row or fillWidth for a column when the content benefits from shared edges.
Designers consume public patterns and component slots; hidden Subcomponents are anatomy references.

inContext.title: Place the primitive where the relationship happens
inContext.description: Use Stack in the slot owned by a public component, where direction and gap carry product meaning.
blocks: Use a vertical Stack when actions belong under supporting copy.
Use horizontal direction when actions are a deliberate row.
Let the component own the slot
A public ActionFooter or related component gives this primitive its product meaning.

doDont.title: Protect structure and clarity
doDont.description: These pairs keep Stack focused on one public slot and one intentional direction.
blocks: Let a vertical slot fill its width
Use fill width when the children should share the column edge.
Fix child widths when the column should fill
Fixed child dimensions still win, so the column edge no longer aligns.
Use fill width when column edges should align
Vertical children can share the stack width when they support stretch.
Use Stack as a catch-all page canvas
Stack has no wrap, padding, or overlap semantics for unrelated sections.

sources.title: Grounded in the published component
sources.description: The guide separates designer choices from behavior supplied by the public library at runtime.
blocks: Live layout examples use public exports from jfs-components 0.1.60. Stack uses its public package export with token-driven modes; documentation controls change owner configuration, not component internals.
